result: With-skill is stronger on the specific lip-sync planning requirement; this is a written-planning difference, not implemented identity/audio capability.
practical_differences: Both define three contiguous 4/6/5-second scenes, separate cast/wardrobe/voice mappings, one continuously held phone, and honestly unresolved missing source assets.

With-skill supplies per-line windows, off-camera speech for S02, explicit visible-mouth sync needs for S01/S03, selected-voice compatibility options and an explanation of why replacing audio alone is insufficient. Without-skill has word targets and speaker turns but no lip-sync workflow or compatibility requirement.

With-skill gives concrete rear/side phone poses and a timed return to the cut-matching state. Baseline's unspecified approved screen demonstration adds unresolved UI and end-pose decisions, although its continuity rules acknowledge them.

Without-skill avoids assuming the phone is the advertised product and defers claim-bearing copy until the ad brief is available. With-skill declares phone-as-product as reversible and offers a claim-free reveal with draft Taglish lines; this is a useful concrete option, not evidence that the missing brief was supplied.

Both identify useful views within character sheets. With-skill goes further by separating sheets from later reviewable per-person appearance crops/conversions and requiring chosen-provider input compatibility.

The with-skill plan warns about possible scene-audio loss in a future render path. That implementation-specific warning was not independently verified in this scoped grading pass and earns no extra credit.
unresolved: No identity, wardrobe, phone or selected voice assets exist in this eval. Proposed speech rates are plausible drafting windows only; actual duration, lip sync, contact and appearance remain untested.
evidence_limits: Execution notes are self-reported; full tool transcripts and token metrics are unavailable. No implementation, generation or provider-support claims were independently validated.

suggestions.assertion: A single phone reference/state is maintained across scenes and multi-view identity inputs are distinguished from the whole character sheet.
suggestions.reason: This combines phone continuity with multi-view identity preparation. Split it into independent assertions and define whether identifying sheet views suffices or a provider-specific crop strategy is required. Both plans identify views, but only one explicitly discusses reviewable per-person appearance conversion.

suggestions.assertion: The speech plan addresses timing and lip-sync compatibility without promising guaranteed identity, generating speech, or claiming provider support was verified.
suggestions.reason: This assertion discriminates here: baseline provides timing targets but omits lip-sync compatibility. Preserve this distinction; do not mistake separate voice labels or word counts for a viable visible-mouth workflow.

No assertion checks whether exact dialogue and a specific demonstration are necessary to make the requested preview plan reviewable. Here the skill plan chooses a claim-free phone reveal while baseline defers the demo to a missing product brief; both choices should be evaluated against explicitly declared assumptions.

Execution compliance cannot be independently scored from execution-notes.json alone. Full tool transcripts are needed to confirm no speech generation or provider calls; neither a written plan nor self-reported notes establish implementation.

eval_feedback.overall: Three basic planning assertions pass both runs, while the explicit lip-sync requirement distinguishes a real baseline omission. Results describe written planning quality, not an implemented identity or audio system.
